top.title: Xenophobic attacks: Help South Africans, don’t punish them — OAU don
top.description: …As varsity’s International Relations Department marks 50th anniversary By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Federal Government has been urged to adopt a sympathetic approach towards South Africa over the recent xenophobic attacks, rather than resort to punitive measures, with a don at the Obafemi Awolowo University (OAU), Ile-Ife, saying South Africans need help at a difficult time. A Professor of International Relations at OAU, Charles Ukeje, said the xenophobic violence was regrettable, particularly given Nigeria’s significant contributions, alongside other African countries, to the struggle against apartheid in South Africa. Ukeje spoke during a press conference organised to herald the 50th anniversary of the university’s Department of International Relations at the campus. He blamed the attacks partly on the failure of successive South African governments to adequately educate their citizens about the sacrifices made by Nigeria and other African countries towards ending apartheid. According to him, proper education about the contributions of other African nations could have helped foster a stronger sense of brotherhood among South Africans and other Africans. He said: “I believe that the xenophobic violence in South Africa is very regrettable. It is regrettable because this is a country which the rest of the continent, particularly Nigeria, helped to midwife in the context of apartheid. “So, in the post-apartheid era, you would expect that the South Africans will be more and better disposed to the rest of Africans, given the amount of sacrifice that Nigerians and other African countries have made in the bid to end apartheid in that country. “It is regrettable that generations of South African leaders, upon achieving an end to apartheid, really did not adequately educate their citizens on the role the whole of Africa played. “Perhaps, if they had done that, things would have been different. Perhaps, the ordinary South African citizens on the street would treat and see other Africans as brothers.” On Nigeria’s response, the don said the country should maintain its longstanding commitment to Africa as the centrepiece of its foreign policy. top.title: Lagos govt warns PSPs over refuse crisis, demands results
top.description: …..As Solus, Olusosun dumpsites resume operations …PSPs to deploy over 700 trucks By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has warned Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators to deliver immediate results or face enforcement measures, following the reopening of the Solus and Olusosun dumpsites after months of closure. The government said it had fulfilled its responsibility by rehabilitating the facilities and their access roads, leaving waste operators with no further excuses for the persistent refuse crisis across the state. Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, gave the warning on Wednesday during an inspection of the previously closed Solus dumpsite in Alimosho Local Government Area. Wahab said the government expected PSP operators to improve waste collection and evacuation across their areas of operation, stressing that residents deserved value for the services they paid for. “Too much is given, so much more is expected. There are no more excuses,” the commissioner said, recounting his message to the leadership of the PSP operators. “The state government has done its own bit; let your PSP members also put their skin in it and see how they can achieve what we set out jointly to achieve because they suggested we put this into play and now we’ve done it for them.” According to him, the decision to reopen Solus followed proposals by waste operators to rehabilitate the facility rather than wait for the development of new dumpsites around Badagry and Epe. He explained that Solus, located within Lagos West, serves several local government areas, including Alimosho, Ajeromi-Ifelodun, Mushin, Badagry, Ikeja, Ojo and Apapa. The commissioner said the contractor handling the rehabilitation had assured the government that the repaired access road would last at least one year, subject to quarterly maintenance. He added that the facility was expected to accommodate at least 100 trucks daily, significantly improving waste evacuation in the affected areas. “100 trucks from this axis coming here to discharge gives us the comfort that our streets, our homes will not be littered with waste,” Wahab said. Addressing complaints by residents over the failure of some PSP operators to collect refuse regularly, the commissioner said the state government would enforce its polluter-pays policy to ensure operators delivered the services for which residents paid. He warned that the government would take necessary measures to hold defaulting operators accountable. LAWMA restructuring Wahab also confirmed a major restructuring of the Lagos Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), ordered by the state governor, as part of efforts to improve waste management operations. He announced the appointment of Juwon Akinyemi as Acting Managing Director, Dr Tjani Olorunwa as Acting Executive Director of Operations, and Kunle Adebiyi as substantive Executive Director of Finance. top.description: Enzo Fernandez and Elliot Anderson both cost Manchester City more than £100m in the summer [Getty Images] The ongoing international break will give Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca much-needed time to fix the growing issues in his squad. The Italian made a dream start after taking over from Pep Guardiola in the summer, leading the club to a record seven consecutive victories at the beginning of the Premier League season. But three consecutive defeats have followed as they have fallen six points adrift of league leaders Arsenal, who are looking in imperious form as they aim to retain their title. In September, it was announced that City had been found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules, and matches have continued as the club await the outcome of their appeal. With possible sanctions hanging over them, is City's recent league form down to psychological issues or are there tactical problems Maresca needs to address? Maresca's dream start turns into nightmare as title hopes hit Property, football and politics: The links between Manchester and Abu Dhabi explained Renowned sports psychologist Dr Paul McCarthy has 25 years' experience working in the industry with top clubs in England, Scotland, Germany and France. McCarthy works on the personal and professional lives of players and says both contribute to how well they perform on the pitch, with the need to "piece together a jigsaw" when situations become disrupted. "Players are like everyone else - they talk about what is going on in their own lives and things that are topical, especially about uncertain events," McCarthy tells BBC Sport. "It generates communication with a lot of stories and rumour and over time if there are enough losses, there often becomes a reduced collective efficacy. "A collective efficacy is a squad's belief in their ability to do what they need to do [to win] and because of their success in the past, that is often shaken a little by consecutive losses." 'Uncertainty leads to a lack of perceived control' City were sitting pretty at the top of the table after a flawless start, but have dropped to third - behind Arsenal and Brighton. After the guilty verdict was announced during the last international break, Maresca's men won their first game back - against 10-man Liverpool at Anfield - then narrowly overcame Ipswich at Etihad Stadium in their following match. But they have since lost to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest, with defensive issues exposed and individual mistakes proving costly. In their first seven games of the season, City did not concede any goals because of individual errors - but that has shifted dramatically in the past three matches, with four mistakes from players contributing to goals. top.title: “You Don’t Have to Worry About Winning the Conference Championship”: Brian Kelly Makes Surprising Admission About College Football’s Future
top.description: Tigers Head Coach Brian Kelly, LSU Tigers take on the Texas A&M Aggies. © Imagn Former LSU head coach Brian Kelly believes the College Football Playoff’s planned expansion to 24 teams in 2027 will bring the biggest shift in how teams define success. Kelly believes winning a conference championship may no longer be the ultimate goal for programs. Instead, securing a place in the expanded playoff field will become their primary focus. Speaking on SiriusXM, Kelly explained how the new format could reshape college football. “You don’t have to worry about winning the conference championship. You need to be one of the 24 teams. And so that’s a paradigm shift in terms of what you’re looking at, in terms of building your football team,” Kelly said. Kelly thinks the expanded playoff will give more programs a realistic opportunity to compete for a national championship. As per the new 24-team format, the playoff field will include the four Power Four conference champions, the highest-ranked Group of Six champion, and 19 teams selected based on the committee’s final rankings. That structure will be significantly beneficial for programs that traditionally struggled to compete financially and recruit at the same level as other teams with bigger budgets. “So it’s now a lot different in terms of what your ultimate goal is. And that’s get in the playoffs,” he added. Alabama’s Ranking Raises Questions About the CFP Selection Criteria The current playoff selection process shows why conference championships and head-to-head results don’t tell the full story. Alabama went up from No. 5 to No. 3 in the CFP rankings despite having two losses. Committee chair Hunter Yurachek defended the decision by saying it’s because of the Crimson Tide’s strength of schedule and four quality wins. “They’re number one in their record strength, number one in their schedule strength. They have four of what we call quality wins, because we continue to call that the win against Mississippi State earlier in the year when they had Kamario Taylor on their team. They were four and zero. Alabama went there and won that game. So Alabama, we believe, deserves to be the number three team in the country,” committee chair Hunter Yurachek said on ESPN. Alabama’s ranking also placed it above Tennessee, despite the Volunteers defeating the Crimson Tide earlier in the season. Yurachek explained that the committee considers the overall resume rather than relying only on head-to-head results. top.title: Stephen A. Smith says Sean McVay has done something ‘inexcusable’ with the LA Rams
top.description: Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have had a mixed 2026/27 season so far after having a lot of hype around them ahead of the campaign. Going into Week 10 of the season they have a 5-4 record and are third in the NFC West. Now, Stephen A. Smith has gone on a rant about Rams coach Sean McVay, first taking issue with how late his team flew to Australia to face the San Francisco 49ers at the start of the season. Speaking via NFL on ESPN , he said: “I have to say to Sean McVay, what has happened to you? What’s happened to you? I think he’s an elite coach. I think he’s big time. He’s a brilliant dude, next level with football, a wonderful dude to talk to, the whole bit. Got nothing but love for him. “I don’t know what the h*** has happened to him this year. You go to Melbourne, Australia, and land 28 hours before kickoff. The 49ers were there for a week. For some reason, you’re the only human being alive, the only adult that I’ve ever known that didn’t take into consideration jet lag and the kind of impact that will have on you.” Stephen A. Smith suggests handling of Puka Nacua amid injuries is ‘some inexcusable stuff’ After that, he questioned the handling of Puka Nacua on the back of his injury issues, suggesting that putting him in a ‘jet-sweep situation’ is ‘inexcusable stuff’. Smith continued: “Sunday, a jet sweep for Puka Nacua, who’s had injuries, on a third-and-11, I believe it was. I mean, what are you calling a jet sweep for? For him? “This is the dude that was healthy enough to play but didn’t want to play because he wasn’t 100%. And you’re going to put him in a position to get compromised health-wise by something other than running a route out in the deep parts of a football field, when your options, because Davante Adams ain’t in there… Because I have to look up these names, because I’ll be d***** if I know them. Konata Mumpfield, right? “Tutu Atwell, you know, Jordan Whittington, Xavier Smith. You ever heard of those names? I mean, y’all get paid to cover football for a living, and you’ve got to look those names up. We don’t know those people. No disrespect to you. I’m quite sure you can play, but we don’t know you. You understand? So, I’m like, what the h*** is going on? “This is what you’ve got to rely upon, you know this, and you’re going to put Puka Nacua in a jet-sweep situation. This is some inexcusable stuff. I don’t know what the h*** is going on with Sean McVay. I love Sean McVay. I don’t understand what has happened to him. I think it’s a little bit too much California sunshine.” The Rams are now due to take on the 3-6 Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, November 15. Should they lose that tie, they will have already matched their losses from the entirety of 2025 when they finished the regular season 12-5. top.title: Newcastle United ready to battle Sunderland in the race for forward
top.description: Newcastle United ready to battle Sunderland in the race for forward Newcastle Scouts Watch Dion Beljo Newcastle United have done the sensible thing here. They have looked, checked, and looked again. According to TeamTalk, club scouts were at the Stadium of Light to watch Dion Beljo as Dinamo Zagreb beat Sunderland 2-0, and the Croatian forward duly did what centre-forwards are paid to do, he scored. That matters. Plenty of strikers can look tidy in clips, rack up flattering numbers in weaker stretches, or disappear when the level rises. Beljo had Premier League eyes on him and still delivered. The report states that “Newcastle and Leeds were both represented on Wearside to watch Beljo in action against Sunderland”, which tells you this was part of a serious information-gathering exercise rather than idle curiosity. Beljo’s output is the headline for a reason. He now has “17 goals in 17 games” this season and an overall senior return of “115 notches from 269 games”. Those are hard numbers, and clubs tend to trust hard numbers more than hype. TeamTalk also notes that Beljo “has been in sensational form for Dinamo”, a fair summary for a striker who appears to be building momentum at exactly the right moment in the market. IMAGO Beljo Transfer Race Growing Fast This is not a one-club chase. Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, Everton, Brighton and Brentford have all been credited with interest, while Sunderland are also said to be paying attention after getting a close-up look themselves. In other words, Newcastle are entering a crowded room, and crowded rooms tend to raise prices. Still, there is logic in Newcastle’s interest. TeamTalk says the club “are seeking more of a presence up front” and want to strengthen Matthias Jaissle’s attacking options. That checks out. Squad building is not about collecting names, it is about profile, availability and role. If Beljo offers size, penalty-box instincts and current form, then he fits the brief of an extra forward who can change games and absorb minutes across a long season. The key line in all this may be that clubs are “gathering information on Croatian hotshot”. That is usually where real transfer business starts. Before bids come the background checks, live viewings, tactical fit discussions and financial modelling. Newcastle have clearly moved into that phase. Why Newcastle Interest Makes Sense There is another point worth making. Watching a player against English opposition is useful, even in European competition, because it gives recruiters a cleaner reference point. Beljo facing Sunderland and scoring in a 2-0 win offered exactly that. As the report puts it, “His latest strike against Sunderland will only have strengthened his reputation, particularly given the number of clubs keeping a close eye on his development.” Newcastle will also know that January deals become awkward when too many clubs are involved. top.title: Joel Embiid Takes Subtle Shot At Jayson Tatum, Opens Up About His Relationship With Paul George
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Joel Embiid and the Philadelphia 76ers dropped to 9-3 in this 2026-27 NBA season after a 123-101 blowout loss to the Boston Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Tuesday. All the talk going into this game was about Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum , and the former getting revenge against the Celtics for trading him, but it was someone else who shone against his former team. Paul George erupted for 36 points (14-22 FG), five rebounds, and one assist against the 76ers, but Embiid didn’t seem too surprised by his former teammate’s performance in his postgame press conference . “He played well,” Embiid said, via PHLY Sports. “He came in here, and that’s what he’s been doing all season. He’s healthy, he’s in a good space mentally. So yeah, I mean, he’s been playing well all season, and he just did what he was doing all season.” George, whom the Celtics acquired for Brown in the summer, is definitely having a good season, and this is the best we’ve seen him play since his time with the Los Angeles Clippers . The nine-time All-Star struggled with injuries during his two seasons with the 76ers, but is doing well physically and mentally on his new team. Now, Tatum and Brown’s relationship had evidently broken down by the time their partnership ended in the summer, but that’s not the case here. Embiid spoke about having a special relationship with George and threw a subtle jab at Tatum in the process. ‘Obviously, Paul is great,” Embiid said. “Off the court, we have a special relationship. Families are close, especially both of our kids. Actually, all of our kids. So yeah, I mean, I love him. I think that’s why I’m extremely happy for him. He’s healthy; he’s playing well. He’s been, from the start of the season, you see what he did tonight; you can kind of say he’s been the best player, to a certain level. “So, yeah, extremely happy for him, proud of him,” Embiid added. “Obviously, we have a good relationship outside of this whole thing, and that’s what matters.” George has been great, but has he been the Celtics’ best player over Tatum? He has struggled a bit with efficiency, but is now averaging 26.5 points, 6.0 rebounds, 7.4 assists, 0.7 steals, and 0.7 blocks per game in 2026-27. He has been a fine second option to Tatum, and these two have the Celtics at the top of the Eastern Conference with a 9-2 record. This might have been the Celtics’ best win of the season, but also the 76ers’ worst defeat. top.description: Cedric Doumbe (right) switched to MMA from kickboxing in 2021 [Getty Images] Cedric Doumbe says it is "crazy" he will get the chance to "face my boss and knock him out" when he fights Jake Paul in Dubai on 24 December. Doumbe is signed to the Professional Fighters League (PFL) - an MMA organisation that Paul's Most Valuable Promotions merged with in July. The pair will fight on Christmas Eve in Paul's first bout since being stopped by former world heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua last December. In a news conference in Paris to promote the event, Cameroonian-born Frenchman Doumbe thanked MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian for his role in setting up the fight against Paul. "I want to thank Nakisa. He's the boss. And Jake, he's the boss, too. I want to thank Nakisa, because that's the first time I will face my boss and knock him out," said Doumbe. "My boss will pay me to knock him out. That's crazy. We never see that before." The fight against 29-year-old American Paul is a professionally sanctioned eight-round cruiserweight boxing bout with the fighters using 10oz gloves. Paul, who is a social media influencer turned professional fighter, has won 12 of his 14 fights as a professional, with his two defeats coming against Tommy Fury and Joshua. Doumbe, 34, is a former kickboxing world champion who has won two of his three fights since joining the PFL in 2023. Despite having just one professional boxing bout to his name, which he won in 2015, Doumbe says he's "watching videos on Netflix" instead of training for the fight because he regards Paul as a "joke". "I do nothing. I just watch videos on Netflix. I just want this fight, this clown fight. I have everything to beat this guy," said Doumbe. "This guy is a joke. He's a very great YouTuber, but he's not a fighter. He's not even a good boxer. I just need to lose weight to face this guy, that's why I'm training now." Paul had to have two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed after having his jaw broken by Joshua - an injury which left his career in doubt. Last week Paul said on social media he would retire if he lost to Doumbe, before confirming his plans in the news conference. "I'm 100% retiring if I lose to this guy. For sure," said Paul. "He's never been in there with someone like me in boxing. It's a completely different sport, that's what he doesn't understand. Fonseca views the Brazilian as a crucial addition to his new squad in Portugal. The club hierarchy have listened to their coach and have already initiated formal steps to welcome the player to Lisbon in the upcoming window. A move to Sporting would allow Endrick to reunite with a manager he knows extremely well. Fonseca previously recruited the talented attacker during his spell at Lyon last season, leading to a highly fruitful collaboration between the pair. Champions League draw and guaranteed minutes The prospect of linking up with his former Lyon boss is a significant factor for Endrick. Rejoining a coach who completely understands his profile and tactical strengths could provide the perfect environment to restart his season. The Italian outfit remain firmly in the race and could complicate the Portuguese club's transfer plans. A temporary switch would allow Endrick to gain vital experience while remaining tied to his parent club.

top.title: Roman Anthony Injury Update: Red Sox CBO Outlines Recovery Plan for $130M Boston Star
top.description: Roman Anthony. © USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Boston Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow provided an encouraging update on Roman Anthony’s right hand and wrist injury. At Monday’s MLB general managers’ meeting in Las Vegas, Breslow said Anthony’s injury is taking longer to recover from than expected. Anthony, who is signed to an eight-year, $130 million contract, is expected to recover during the offseason. On Tuesday, Breslow joined NESN’s 310 To Left podcast and shared Anthony’s offseason recovery plan. “Yeah, he’s in the midst of, you know, just a period of time where we wanted him to rest and just minimize any of the stress that he might put on his wrist,” Breslow said. “He’s going to be evaluated in a few weeks, at which point we’re hopeful that he can start to take on a strengthening program and get some of the range of motion back before ultimately starting a hitting progression.” Anthony initially injured his right ring finger on May 4 against the Detroit Tigers. He suffered a partially torn carpometacarpal (CMC) ligament, which connects the base of his right ring finger to his wrist. The Red Sox star missed nearly four months before returning on Aug. 30. Anthony’s injury resurfaced during Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series against the Yankees on September 29. The subsequent imaging revealed new muscle strains in his right wrist, leading to Anthony’s removal from the postseason roster. Later, the Red Sox star admitted that when he first returned in August, he still felt discomfort in his hand, but he risked playing through the injury. Red Sox Rule Out Surgery For Roman Anthony While Craig Breslow admitted that the diagnosis has not changed for Roman Anthony as of now, the need for surgery has been ruled out. Breslow cited Anthony’s multiple follow-up appointments and imaging tests and revealed that the Red Sox outfielder will not need any offseason procedure. “Yeah, he’s had a bunch of follow-up appointments here, including imaging,” Breslow said via MLB.com . “We’re still collecting information, still working through what the kind of right course of treatment is. And at this point, it doesn’t seem that there’s any type of surgical intervention. It looks like rest is likely the best path to recovery.” Because of the wrist injury, Anthony could only take 242 plate appearances, finishing with an OPS of just .735. With Anthony set to be re-evaluated in a couple of weeks, the Red Sox hope the outfielder will be ready to participate in spring training in 2027. nigeria.description: …..As Solus, Olusosun dumpsites resume operations …PSPs to deploy over 700 trucks By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has warned Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators to deliver immediate results or face enforcement measures, following the reopening of the Solus and Olusosun dumpsites after months of closure. The government said it had fulfilled its responsibility by rehabilitating the facilities and their access roads, leaving waste operators with no further excuses for the persistent refuse crisis across the state. He explained that Solus, located within Lagos West, serves several local government areas, including Alimosho, Ajeromi-Ifelodun, Mushin, Badagry, Ikeja, Ojo and Apapa. The commissioner said the contractor handling the rehabilitation had assured the government that the repaired access road would last at least one year, subject to quarterly maintenance. He added that the facility was expected to accommodate at least 100 trucks daily, significantly improving waste evacuation in the affected areas. “100 trucks from this axis coming here to discharge gives us the comfort that our streets, our homes will not be littered with waste,” Wahab said. Addressing complaints by residents over the failure of some PSP operators to collect refuse regularly, the commissioner said the state government would enforce its polluter-pays policy to ensure operators delivered the services for which residents paid. He warned that the government would take necessary measures to hold defaulting operators accountable. nigeria.title: Police probe Blord over armed officers’ escort
nigeria.description: The Nigeria Police Force has launched an investigation into a viral video showing armed police officers escorting businessman Linus Williams, popularly known as Blord, at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, described the deployment of the officers as “unlawful and illegal”, saying an investigation had commenced into the incident. Iniedu disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X account on Wednesday while reacting to the video. “Unlawful and illegal. Investigation has commenced into this incident please. We say #notoimpunity,” he wrote. The video, which Blord shared on his Instagram page on Tuesday, showed him arriving at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Enugu, accompanied by armed police officers dressed in camouflage uniforms and tactical gear. The businessman was seen wearing a red-and-white striped traditional cap associated with the Kwankwaso political brand. He was also seen arriving in a black Cadillac with the personalised number plate, “B-LORD”. Other scenes in the footage showed Blord walking alongside the armed officers at the airport and at other locations, including what appeared to be his business premises. The officers were seen providing him with an escort and opening the vehicle door for him. Captioning the video, Blord wrote: “Back to base, business as usual. From the airport to a brief stop at BlordGroup Enugu branch, then back to Awka. Every move has its purpose, and the vision never takes a break. Blord is home!” In another Instagram post, the businessman said he had been in Sabon Gari, Kano State, where he met his “brothers” before returning to Enugu. The development comes months after President Bola Tinubu ordered the withdrawal of police officers attached to Very Important Persons (VIPs) across the country and their redeployment to core policing duties. Tinubu gave the directive at a security meeting with service chiefs and the Director-General of the Department of State Services in Abuja on November 23, 2025. According to a statement by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, VIPs requiring protection would henceforth be assigned armed operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps instead of police officers. The President said the measure was aimed at strengthening police presence in communities, particularly those facing security challenges. On December 6, 2025, the police also deployed a Special Enforcement Team to monitor compliance with the directive, beginning with an operation in Lagos. The then Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Benjamin Hundeyin, said the exercise recorded no cases of unauthorised deployment of police escorts. nigeria.title: Kwankwaso and I have failed if anyone remains in IDP camps after 18 months — Obi
nigeria.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has promised to tackle Nigeria’s displacement crisis, declaring that his administration would have failed if any Nigerian remained in an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp 18 months after assuming office. Obi gave the assurance while speaking in Jos, the Plateau State capital, on Wednesday, where he pledged to prioritise national unity and security if elected president in the 2027 general election. He lamented the divisions among Nigerians along ethnic and religious lines, insisting that national unity was essential to addressing the country’s challenges. According to him, his administration would focus on uniting the country and ensuring the safety of citizens, particularly in communities affected by persistent killings and displacement. “Our commitment is to unite Nigeria because today there is no unity, we are divided along tribal lines, religious lines, and that should not be, we are Nigerians. “Number two is to secure Nigeria. It’s our priority to ensure that Nigerians live in safety. In a place like Plateau and Benue where people are being killed daily, I assure you that no mother will cry again for her children. I assure you that no woman will feel the pain of losing a husband, neither will the father feel the pain of losing a wife,” he said. The former Anambra State governor stressed that his administration would not tolerate a situation in which Nigerians remained displaced long after he assumed office. “I have said it, and I will repeat it that after one year to 18 months in office, if any Nigerian remains in an IDP camp, we have failed,” he declared. Obi, who said he was familiar with the security challenges confronting communities in Plateau State, cited his visits to Bokkos, Mangu and Barkin Ladi as evidence of his understanding of the plight of affected residents. “No other presidential candidate has been to Bokkos, Mangu, and Barkin Ladi, so I know the pain that people are going through,” he said. He also expressed confidence that a joint administration with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as vice-president would tackle kidnapping and insecurity across the country. “Let me assure you that with Kwankwaso and I as the president and vice president of this country, nobody will kidnap school children and go into the bush,” Obi said. nigeria.title: Brazil Electoral Court Fines Meta $1.3mn In Lula-Bolsonaro Spat
nigeria.description: Brazil’s electoral court ruled Tuesday that Meta had to pay a fine of about $1.3 million for failing to comply with court orders after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva alleged the tech giant tipped the scales toward his rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, during the latest presidential election. Leftist leader Lula had accused Meta of “algorithmic manipulation” favoring Bolsonaro in the run-up to the October 25 runoff vote, in which he surprisingly prevailed despite coming in second during the first-round ballot. Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva gestures during a meeting of the National Council for the Industrialisation of Critical and Strategic Minerals at the Planalto Palace in Brasília on November 5, 2026. (Photo by Evaristo Sa / AFP) | Evaristo Sa / AFP The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unanimously ruled to impose a fine of 7.5 million reais (around $1.3 million) on Meta, the parent company of Facebook, WhatsApp and Telegram, finding the company missed deadlines and lacked transparency in its investigation. However, the court’s reporting judge Marco Aurelio said the judicial body had not found evidence of any “deliberate action to skew the election.” This illustration photograph shows the Brazilian flag displayed on a smartphone screen in front of a screen displaying the logo of US technology company Meta in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on October 19, 2026. Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP Meta had denied the accusations but acknowledged that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors. “We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula said of social media companies after his electoral victory. After refusing to acknowledge his loss in the runoff, Flavio Bolsonaro fled Brazil to the United States amid an ongoing investigation into him for alleged money laundering. nigeria.title: Tinubu: Anambra RHA mobilises 143,000 vote canvassers
nigeria.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Renewed Hope Ambassadors (RHA) in Anambra State have mobilised no fewer than 143,000 vote canvassers across the state’s 5,720 polling units to campaign for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections. The state coordinator of RHA, Chief Okey Ezenwa, disclosed this during a meeting of the organisation’s zonal and local government coordinators. Ezenwa said each polling unit had 25 canvassers prepared to drive grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election. “The Anambra State chapter of RHA is fully prepared for the 16 January 2027 presidential election. Our coordinators are fully on ground in the 21 Local Government Areas and the 326 wards,” he said. He disclosed that an 11-member local government committee and a 10-member ward steering committee had also been established to strengthen the organisation’s coordination and mobilisation efforts. According to him, the meeting resolved to convene a separate meeting with all APC National Assembly and State Assembly candidates in Anambra to agree on a clear strategic direction, particularly amid concerns over the perceived inactivity of the party’s state chapter. Ezenwa reaffirmed that the RHA would serve as a major political structure supporting APC candidates in the presidential, National Assembly and State Assembly elections. He also directed zonal, local government and ward coordinators to intensify grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu’s re-election. The RHA coordinator expressed the organisation’s commitment to mobilising support for the successful conduct of the forthcoming presidential campaign rallies in the state. He commended the Director-General of RHA and Governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodimma, for his efforts in mobilising support for President Tinubu across the country. nigeria.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases
nigeria.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo’s worst-ever outbreak of Ebola has now reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases, official Congolese figures showed on Wednesday, as armed conflict hampers the response. The 17th outbreak of the virus in the DRC’s history was officially declared in May but experts believe it emerged weeks or even months earlier. It has infected 11,042 people in the DRC and caused 5,387 deaths, according to the National Institute of Public Health. Around 2,990 people have recovered from Ebola, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever. Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the last 50 years. The worst outbreak previously recorded in the DRC killed nearly 2,300 people out of 3,500 cases between 2018 and 2020. The latest outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. No approved vaccines or treatments exist currently for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the latest outbreak. Last month, the World Health Organization announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, would be put through a full human trial in the DRC to see if it offered any cross-protection against Bundibugyo. Security in eastern DRC is another challenge in fighting the health crisis. Ituri province is one of the most volatile and clashes between armed groups and violence against health workers regularly occur. A health centre treating Ebola patients was set on fire on Sunday by youths in Lolwa in Ituri province, health authorities said. Clashes between local militia on the same day temporarily suspended the health response in the area of Fataki, according to the UN. Islamic State-affiliated rebels from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) have carried out deadly attacks in several areas of Ituri, Haut-Uele and North Kivu in recent days, local and security sources said. nigeria.title: ADC cannot stop Tinubu, APC will win all 36 states — Adeyeye
nigeria.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — The Chairman of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Senator Dayo Adeyeye, has dismissed the African Democratic Congress (ADC) as a serious threat to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, predicting that the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) will win all 36 states. Adeyeye, who is also the National Chairman of the South-West Agenda for Asiwaju (SWAGA), said the ADC lacked the political structure, grassroots influence and electoral strength to challenge the ruling party. He also questioned the political strength of the ADC’s presidential candidate, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, alleging that he lacked sufficient support even in his home state of Adamawa. Adeyeye spoke with journalists in Ado-Ekiti on Wednesday while assessing the political landscape ahead of the 2027 general election. He dismissed suggestions that the APC was apprehensive about the opposition, describing such claims as unfounded. According to him, the ADC has yet to demonstrate sufficient political strength at the state and National Assembly levels to pose a credible challenge to the ruling party. “How can the APC be afraid of anything with the political atmosphere we have now? I said over three months ago that President Tinubu was likely to win all the 36 states, and I am becoming increasingly convinced that it will happen. “ADC is a party without a governor in any of the 36 states. How many members does it have in the National Assembly? How many state assemblies does it control? You cannot compare a party without a demonstrable political structure with the APC,” he said. The former senator argued that Atiku’s presidential ambition was further weakened by what he described as inadequate political backing in Adamawa State. He alleged that neither the state governor nor prominent political figures in Adamawa had demonstrated substantial support for the former vice-president. “Atiku is from Adamawa, but the governor of his state is not supporting him. The legislature in the state has not witnessed any significant movement to the ADC. How do you intend to challenge and defeat an incumbent president when you cannot establish a formidable political base in your own state?” he asked. Adeyeye said SWAGA was established to consolidate Tinubu’s political base in the South-West, stressing that strong support at home was essential for any presidential candidate seeking national acceptance. He maintained that Tinubu had built a formidable political foundation across the South-West, adding that the president’s support base had continued to expand beyond the region. On the economy, Adeyeye acknowledged the hardship facing Nigerians but argued that the removal of fuel subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market had prevented the country from sliding into a deeper economic crisis. nigeria.title: Customs intercepts six pangolins, two die in Oyo
nigeria.description: By Godwin Oritse The Federal Operations Unit (FOU), Zone ‘A’, of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has intercepted six pangolins at Eruwa-Oni in Oyo State in a renewed crackdown on the illegal trafficking of endangered wildlife species. The interception, which took place at about 3 a.m. on Sunday, November 8, 2026, followed an intelligence-led patrol by Customs operatives. The suspected traffickers reportedly abandoned the animals and fled upon sighting the patrol team. The six pangolins were recovered alive and transported to the Unit’s headquarters in Ikeja, Lagos. However, two died shortly after arrival, leaving four surviving animals. The Customs Service subsequently handed over the four surviving pangolins and the carcasses of the two dead animals to relevant wildlife authorities for documentation and further necessary action. The handover was conducted by the Deputy Comptroller in charge of Enforcement, DC A.O. Oguntuase, on behalf of the Comptroller of FOU Zone ‘A’, Lagos. The Unit reiterated that protecting endangered species was a shared responsibility and urged members of the public to provide credible and timely information to assist law enforcement agencies in identifying and apprehending those involved in the illegal capture, possession, transportation and trafficking of protected wildlife. It also reaffirmed its commitment to suppressing smuggling and other forms of illicit trade, while strengthening collaboration with relevant agencies to protect Nigeria’s natural heritage. nigeria.title: Awujale palace not under siege – Ogun police
nigeria.description: The Police Command in Ogun has dismissed reports alleging that the Awujale Palace in Ijebu-Ode was under siege by thugs and miscreants. This is contained in a statement issued by DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the command’s spokesperson in Abeokuta on Wednesday. According to Babaseyi, the deployment is a preventive security measure aimed at safeguarding lives and property and preventing any breakdown of public peace. He added that an Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) was deployed to supervise and coordinate the security arrangement at the palace. The police spokesperson also clarified that one person had been invited following a written petition containing allegations against him. According to him, the person honoured the invitation, was questioned over the allegations and subsequently released on self-recognisance, while investigations continued. Babaseyi stressed that the invitation was part of a legitimate investigative process and should not be interpreted as an indication of guilt. He reiterated the command’s commitment to professionalism, impartiality, the rule of law and respect for the rights of all individuals. “Members of the public should remain calm, disregard misleading reports and avoid circulating unverified information capable of creating tension or disturbing public peace. “The command is committed to protecting lives and property, maintaining public order and enforcing the law impartially across the state,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the Awujale stool became vacant in July 2025, following the death of Oba Sikiru Adetona at 91, after 65 years reign. nigeria.title: Fossil Fuels ‘Must Go The Way Of The Dinosaurs’, UN Chief Tells World Leaders At COP31
nigeria.description: UN chief Antonio Guterres on Wednesday accused oil and gas interests of blocking action on climate change and urged world leaders at COP31 to “end the fossil fuel addiction”. “Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs, but that won’t happen on its own. The dinosaurs did not have a lobby, but fossil fuels do,” Guterres said in Turkey at his final UN climate summit as secretary-general. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres railed against the oil and gas lobby on Wednesday, urging world leaders to “end the fossil fuel addiction” at a climate summit missing several prominent figures. The two-week COP31 talks kicked off in Turkey earlier this week with governments under pressure to tackle climate change after a year of searing heatwaves and wildfires in Europe, and deadly floods in Nepal. “The brutal truth is that the climate crisis is outrunning us,” Guterres told dozens of world leaders assembled at a sprawling expo centre in the Mediterranean city of Antalya. This handout photograph taken and released by Turkish Presidency Press Office on November 10, 2026, shows Turkey’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan (C,R) meeting with UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres (C,L) during the COP31 UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya. But few major breakthroughs are anticipated at the COP31 negotiations, which run until November 20, as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions fuelled by the US war with Iran and Russia’s conflict in Ukraine. Since agreeing in 2023 for the first time to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver of climate change — nations have struggled to advance that goal at the annual COP conferences. “Fossil fuel interests keep making a killing, while killing our planet,” Guterres said, urging governments to tax the windfall profits of oil companies. “Fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs, but that won’t happen on its own. The dinosaurs did not have a lobby, but fossil fuels do,” he said. “Their strategy is simple: Distort the science. Delay the policy. Delay the action. Delay the accountability. It’s time to kick the habit –- and end the fossil fuel addiction,” he said to applause. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg arrives at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall slightly in 2026 due to the expansion of renewable energy and the oil price shock sparked by the Iran war, researchers said Tuesday. nigeria.title: El Nino Fuels Indonesia Fire Outbreak, Destroys 2.88 Million Hectares – Report
nigeria.description: Fires in Indonesia driven partly by a strong El Nino have burned through 2.88 million hectares (7.1 million acres) so far in 2026, a monitor analysing satellite imagery told AFP on Wednesday. The burned area figure — 18 times the size of London — has increased nearly a million hectares since deforestation monitoring site Nusantara Atlas’s last update in September. Indonesia’s government has not provided official figures for areas burned since announcing 202,000 hectares had been razed by the end of July. The burning detected in analysis through the end of October is a conservative estimate, warned Nusantara Atlas founder David Gaveau, in part because smoke has obscured satellite images. But it already exceeds the full-year figure for 2019, previously the worst year on record in Nusantara Atlas data. Indonesia also experienced devastating fires in 2015, but the satellite imagery used then was different, making a direct comparison difficult. Volunteers spray water to extinguish a land fire at Terantang in Barito Kuala regency, South Kalimantan province, on November 7, 2026, following months of forest and land fires. (Photo by MUDA SAGALA / AFP) Still, the scale of destruction is clear, said Gaveau. “Basically, it’s a really bad year,” he said. The arrival of rain has brought some of the worst blazes under control, and monitoring shows the number of so-called hotspots starting to flatten or decline. But the figure for total burned area is likely to rise further given some fires are still burning, and as burn scars previously hidden by smoke become visible to satellites in coming months. Indonesia’s government previously said it needed more time to analyse data before issuing updated figures. AFP has asked for comment on the monitor’s latest data. Indonesia experiences fires every dry season, but this year’s blazes have been particularly severe in part due to an intense drought caused by the El Nino weather pattern. A firefighter sprays water to extinguish a wildfire burning organic-rich peatland, which smolders underground and releases dense smoke in Pulang Pisau Regency, in Central Kalimantan province on November 4, 2026. (Photo by REINA / AFP) Experts say the fires are also the result of decades of deforestation and the drying out of peatlands for plantations, making large swathes of land more vulnerable to flames. The fires have caused devastating local pollution that has sickened hundreds of thousands of people and sent haze into neighbouring countries, including Malaysia and Singapore. nigeria.title: Man United close to deal with Pochettino to become next coach
nigeria.description: Manchester United are reportedly closing in on an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as head coach if the club decides to end his tenure. According to Sky Sports, the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager, who currently coaches the United States national team, is being lined up as Carrick’s potential successor, with discussions between the parties said to be at an advanced stage. Carrick reported to United’s Carrington training ground at around 7:45 am on Wednesday, with uncertainty continuing over his future at Old Trafford. The club’s hierarchy is expected to discuss his position at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday, where chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are scheduled to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The meeting was initially arranged to review United’s performances this season, but Carrick’s position is now expected to feature prominently following the club’s disappointing start to the campaign. Berrada and Wilcox are expected to present their recommendations to Ratcliffe, who oversees football operations at the club, before a final decision is reached on the head coach’s future. Sky Sports News understands that United would have to pay approximately £7m to release Pochettino from his recently signed contract with the United States national team, although the financial requirement is not considered an obstacle to the proposed appointment. Pochettino is reportedly prepared to take over if United decide to make a change, although he is currently scheduled to lead the United States against Haiti on Saturday. Meanwhile, former United captain Roy Keane has criticised Carrick’s leadership following the club’s recent performances. Keane said the under-pressure manager “talks a lot but doesn’t say much” and needs to “get moving” on improving the team after United’s late 4-4 draw against Aston Villa. United’s struggles have increased scrutiny on Carrick, with the club’s management now considering a potential change in the dugout. nigeria.description: The Federal Government has commissioned three Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) infrastructure facilities in Kano State, as part of efforts to expand access to cleaner and cheaper energy and reduce transportation costs. The facilities, developed by Rolling Energy Limited with support from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), comprise a 300,000-standard cubic metres per day Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) distribution hub and a retail station at Tamburawa, Dawakin Kudu Local Government Area, as well as a 21,000-standard cubic metres per day LCNG daughter and retail station at Hotoro, Tarauni LGA. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, said the projects represented the Federal Government’s commitment to translating Nigeria’s abundant gas resources into tangible economic benefits for citizens. Ekpo, who was represented by a senior government official, said the facilities would strengthen gas distribution, deepen penetration in Kano and neighbouring communities, support businesses and transportation, and create new economic opportunities. He said the Tamburawa hub would provide integrated LNG storage, regasification and CNG distribution services, including the capacity to supply daughter stations, while the retail outlets would ensure that the product reached consumers directly. “Together, these three facilities demonstrate the complete philosophy of our domestic gas agenda: building the infrastructure to receive and distribute gas, while simultaneously creating the last-mile outlets that make the product accessible to Nigerians,” he said. Ekpo during the opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily in Kano, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The minister said the projects aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which, according to him, seeks to move the country from policy formulation to the delivery of critical infrastructure. “His charge to us is clear: we must move from policies to projects, from plans to infrastructure, and from gas reserves beneath our soil to affordable energy that actually reaches our homes, businesses, industries and transportation systems,” he said. Ekpo added that government was determined to mobilise private sector investment to accelerate the development of the country’s gas infrastructure. He commended Rolling Energy, MDGIF, regulators, investors and other technical partners for their contributions to the projects. Ismaeel Ahmed, said the expansion of CNG infrastructure across the country showed that investments in the sector were yielding results. business.title: LNbits Releases 1.7.0 Urgent Security Update After November 8 Attacks Drain Funds
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine LNbits Releases 1.7.0 Urgent Security Update After November 8 Attacks Drain Funds LNbits, the open-source Lightning Network wallet and accounts platform, released version 1.7.0 on November 10 as an urgent security update and instructed all operators to upgrade before restarting their servers. The project’s official X account posted the announcement with a link to the GitHub release , calling it a “SECURITY UPDATE”. The release follows a wave of attacks that began over the weekend. On November 8, LNbits posted on X that all users should stop their LNbits servers immediately after reporting active attacks, adding that security patches were being prepared and that it was “better to err on the side of caution.” The project also disabled instances on its hosted service. Multiple reports documented unauthorized account creation and fund withdrawals. Kevin Ravensberg , operator of the Telegram tipping service BitTipBot, publicly stated that attackers created new accounts on his instance and withdrew 2,285,545 satoshis (approximately 0.0229 BTC) between roughly 09:22 and 14:00 UTC on November 8. According to the official upgrade guidance published alongside the release, versions prior to 1.7.0 are affected and “funds running on prior versions of LNbits are at risk of being stolen.” The project stated that 1.7.0 includes security fixes in response to the incident discovered on November 8 and that a full technical report on the exploit will follow. Operators are advised to set up a fresh server if compromise is suspected, because updating alone cannot remove access an attacker may already have gained. Additional recovery steps include rotating all user wallet keys as Super Admin, replacing funding-source credentials (API keys or macaroons), rotating other secrets stored in settings, and reviewing or re-creating connections for extensions such as NWC Provider, LNDHub, Bolt Cards, TPOS, Bleskomat, and FOSSA. The GitHub release notes describe extensive security hardening across authentication, extension management, and payment handling, plus dependency updates. New features shipping with the version include on-chain wallet support, BOLT12 offer payments, TOTP two-factor authentication, NIP-17 support, a job scheduler, automatic extension updates, and hold invoice support for the LNbits funding source. The project notes that LNbits functions as a hot wallet and that operators should keep only operational balances online, regularly review activity, and move excess funds to offline keys. LNbits was founded as a free and open-source project in 2019 by Ben Arc and later incorporated a commercial entity to support development. It provides multi-user accounts and a large suite of extensions on top of any Lightning funding source (including LND and Core Lightning). entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. It can reduce the time spent on repetitive tasks and create more room for important responsibilities. The important thing is that you should remain actively involved. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. sports.description: Tigers Head Coach Brian Kelly, LSU Tigers take on the Texas A&M Aggies. © Imagn Former LSU head coach Brian Kelly believes the College Football Playoff’s planned expansion to 24 teams in 2027 will bring the biggest shift in how teams define success. Kelly believes winning a conference championship may no longer be the ultimate goal for programs. Instead, securing a place in the expanded playoff field will become their primary focus. Speaking on SiriusXM, Kelly explained how the new format could reshape college football. “You don’t have to worry about winning the conference championship. You need to be one of the 24 teams. And so that’s a paradigm shift in terms of what you’re looking at, in terms of building your football team,” Kelly said. Kelly thinks the expanded playoff will give more programs a realistic opportunity to compete for a national championship. As per the new 24-team format, the playoff field will include the four Power Four conference champions, the highest-ranked Group of Six champion, and 19 teams selected based on the committee’s final rankings. That structure will be significantly beneficial for programs that traditionally struggled to compete financially and recruit at the same level as other teams with bigger budgets. “So it’s now a lot different in terms of what your ultimate goal is. And that’s get in the playoffs,” he added. Alabama’s Ranking Raises Questions About the CFP Selection Criteria The current playoff selection process shows why conference championships and head-to-head results don’t tell the full story. Alabama went up from No. 5 to No. 3 in the CFP rankings despite having two losses. Committee chair Hunter Yurachek defended the decision by saying it’s because of the Crimson Tide’s strength of schedule and four quality wins. “They’re number one in their record strength, number one in their schedule strength. They have four of what we call quality wins, because we continue to call that the win against Mississippi State earlier in the year when they had Kamario Taylor on their team. They were four and zero. Alabama went there and won that game. So Alabama, we believe, deserves to be the number three team in the country,” committee chair Hunter Yurachek said on ESPN. Alabama’s ranking also placed it above Tennessee, despite the Volunteers defeating the Crimson Tide earlier in the season. Yurachek explained that the committee considers the overall resume rather than relying only on head-to-head results. sports.title: 'Crazy' I'll get to 'knock my boss out' - Doumbe
sports.description: Cedric Doumbe (right) switched to MMA from kickboxing in 2021 [Getty Images] Cedric Doumbe says it is "crazy" he will get the chance to "face my boss and knock him out" when he fights Jake Paul in Dubai on 24 December. Doumbe is signed to the Professional Fighters League (PFL) - an MMA organisation that Paul's Most Valuable Promotions merged with in July. The pair will fight on Christmas Eve in Paul's first bout since being stopped by former world heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua last December. In a news conference in Paris to promote the event, Cameroonian-born Frenchman Doumbe thanked MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian for his role in setting up the fight against Paul. "I want to thank Nakisa. He's the boss. And Jake, he's the boss, too. I want to thank Nakisa, because that's the first time I will face my boss and knock him out," said Doumbe. "My boss will pay me to knock him out. That's crazy. We never see that before." The fight against 29-year-old American Paul is a professionally sanctioned eight-round cruiserweight boxing bout with the fighters using 10oz gloves. Paul, who is a social media influencer turned professional fighter, has won 12 of his 14 fights as a professional, with his two defeats coming against Tommy Fury and Joshua. Doumbe, 34, is a former kickboxing world champion who has won two of his three fights since joining the PFL in 2023. Despite having just one professional boxing bout to his name, which he won in 2015, Doumbe says he's "watching videos on Netflix" instead of training for the fight because he regards Paul as a "joke". "I do nothing. I just watch videos on Netflix. I just want this fight, this clown fight. I have everything to beat this guy," said Doumbe. "This guy is a joke. He's a very great YouTuber, but he's not a fighter. He's not even a good boxer. I just need to lose weight to face this guy, that's why I'm training now." Paul had to have two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed after having his jaw broken by Joshua - an injury which left his career in doubt. Last week Paul said on social media he would retire if he lost to Doumbe, before confirming his plans in the news conference. "I'm 100% retiring if I lose to this guy. For sure," said Paul. "He's never been in there with someone like me in boxing. It's a completely different sport, that's what he doesn't understand. "I know he's going to bring a tough fight, but it's just not going to be enough, and that's it at the end of the day." sports.title: Roman Anthony Injury Update: Red Sox CBO Outlines Recovery Plan for $130M Boston Star
sports.description: Roman Anthony. © USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Boston Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow provided an encouraging update on Roman Anthony’s right hand and wrist injury. At Monday’s MLB general managers’ meeting in Las Vegas, Breslow said Anthony’s injury is taking longer to recover from than expected. Anthony, who is signed to an eight-year, $130 million contract, is expected to recover during the offseason. On Tuesday, Breslow joined NESN’s 310 To Left podcast and shared Anthony’s offseason recovery plan. “Yeah, he’s in the midst of, you know, just a period of time where we wanted him to rest and just minimize any of the stress that he might put on his wrist,” Breslow said. “He’s going to be evaluated in a few weeks, at which point we’re hopeful that he can start to take on a strengthening program and get some of the range of motion back before ultimately starting a hitting progression.” Anthony initially injured his right ring finger on May 4 against the Detroit Tigers. He suffered a partially torn carpometacarpal (CMC) ligament, which connects the base of his right ring finger to his wrist. The Red Sox star missed nearly four months before returning on Aug. 30. Anthony’s injury resurfaced during Game 1 of the AL Wild Card Series against the Yankees on September 29. The subsequent imaging revealed new muscle strains in his right wrist, leading to Anthony’s removal from the postseason roster. Later, the Red Sox star admitted that when he first returned in August, he still felt discomfort in his hand, but he risked playing through the injury. Red Sox Rule Out Surgery For Roman Anthony While Craig Breslow admitted that the diagnosis has not changed for Roman Anthony as of now, the need for surgery has been ruled out. Breslow cited Anthony’s multiple follow-up appointments and imaging tests and revealed that the Red Sox outfielder will not need any offseason procedure. “Yeah, he’s had a bunch of follow-up appointments here, including imaging,” Breslow said via MLB.com . “We’re still collecting information, still working through what the kind of right course of treatment is. And at this point, it doesn’t seem that there’s any type of surgical intervention. It looks like rest is likely the best path to recovery.” Because of the wrist injury, Anthony could only take 242 plate appearances, finishing with an OPS of just .735. With Anthony set to be re-evaluated in a couple of weeks, the Red Sox hope the outfielder will be ready to participate in spring training in 2027. technology.title: Google gooses Python AI performance by... removing Python
technology.description: "Train in Python, serve in C++" might as well be Google's motto when it comes to much of its ML work. Python is easy for data scientists to wield, but keeping its interpreter in the serving pipeline can add overhead and deployment headaches. The industry-backed OpenXLA Project provides tools for compiling machine learning computations into native code for different processors. The latest component of this setup to be open sourced is XSE , short for the XLA Serving Engine. One-shot inference XSE is not so much suited for large-scale LLM inference (which would be better served by vLLM or SGLang ), but rather for smaller, more sharply task-oriented models, of which there are plenty at Google. "LLM serving gets most of the attention right now, but a significant amount of production inference is still ranking, recommendation, embedding, and vision models. These tend to be short requests with very high [queries-per-second] and tight latency budgets," Nathan Beach , Google director of product management, wrote in a LinkedIn missive Tuesday. At Google, XSE already handles more than six million queries per second across services including YouTube Shorts, Google Ads, and Search. These models aren't there for a leisurely chat. They rank results, recommend videos, and make other decisions on the fly, often without users noticing. A Python interpreter mulling each request would be a bottleneck, if not the end of Google itself. In Google's tests on short requests, XSE delivered two to five times the throughput of its best optimized Python server, using a quarter of the memory. No Python here In this setup, the ML boffins write their model code in Python, using Google's JAX to help with the sums. Google also plans integration with TorchTPU so PyTorch users can export models for C++ serving on TPUs. An export tool packages the model's computations in StableHLO, a portable intermediate representation, alongside its trained weights in an "XLA SavedModel." Ready to precognate, the C++ serving runtime uses XLA to compile those computations into native code for the target silicon. No Python interpreter to see here. XLA SavedModels can run on GPUs and CPUs – Google partnered with both Arm and Intel to develop the XLA ecosystem. But Google obviously thinks it'd be a lot cooler if you ran your models on its own line of TPU accelerators . Python's sluggishness continues to be an issue for the ML community. Beyond XSE, other approaches have been taken, many of which involve jettisoning the Python code as quickly as possible. PyTorch offers a native C++ runtime called LibTorch . Also, Microsoft and its collaborators offer the ONNX Runtime , which supports an open graph format with Python bindings. Even Python's own reference implementation relies heavily on C, with Rust now getting a foot in the door. ®

technology.title: Linux joins Heathrow's grounded fleet of information screens
technology.description: UK travelers had more than fog to contend with this week, as Linux proved that if Windows could bork anything, it could bork it better. Spotted by Andy Hinks at Heathrow Airport's Terminal 2, this information display has seen better days. While its neighbors offer walking times and terminal maps, it presents a sideways Linux boot log – useful only if your next connection involves mounting a filesystem. There aren't many clues to what has befallen the machine behind the screen. The boot messages mention systemd , an Intel PRO/1000 network adapter, and an EXT4 filesystem on what appears to be a logical volume named LV_ROOT . Whether mounting that filesystem is the problem, or simply the last thing displayed before something else went wrong, isn't clear. Heathrow's information displays clearly accommodate a mixture of technologies. Recent examples ran Microsoft Windows, which had - naturally - suffered a moment of its own. Linux can evidently be just as unreliable in the right hands. The question is which Linux distribution is having its moment in the sun. Heathrow has been rolling out Raspberry Pi-based signage, although the Intel PRO/1000 adapter leaves the hardware behind this particular display something of a mystery. Pi hardware makes sense for signage: it's relatively cheap – at least until AI ate all the RAM – and low-powered compared with a full-fat Windows PC. Heathrow's senior product owner for displays described the approach as a "reliable, secure solution that has a significantly lower hardware cost and are 30-40% more energy efficient than our previous hardware." Readers might be interested to know that Heathrow has spent years working on its new screens. The product owner again: "We've completely re-engineered our content distribution system to be flexible and device-agnostic." So Windows in one place, and Linux somewhere else. All rubbing along famously. Assuming, of course, the displays can show more than a virtual cough and splutter during boot. ®

technology.title: AMD: Where we're going we don't need (as much) DRAM
technology.description: AMD's latest sales pitch: Up to 99 percent of the performance with half the DRAM, provided you're willing to buy a Mext license alongside your shiny new Epyc server. This is made possible by using AI models to load memory pages in and out of cheaper NVMe storage before your operating system or apps ever know they need it — kind of like SWAP or a Windows page file, but smarter. AMD acquired the tech from Mext back in June, and according to former CEO Gary Smerdon — now CVP of business development at AMD — the tech could cut enterprise server costs by as much as 83 percent by replacing costly RDIMMs with flash storage. Of the initial 145 systems the software has been deployed on so far, he estimates customers have already saved $5 million in avoided DRAM costs. "Conservatively, 60, 70, even 80 or 90 percent for very large memory systems, of the cost of a server can be in memory," he explained. Everyone's favorite buzzword to the rescue Even in systems with high memory utilization, where (say) 95 percent of the memory is "in use," a lot of it isn't actively being used, he explained. He cited a Meta research paper that showed that between 50 and 80 percent of memory pages hadn't been touched in five minutes, ten minutes, or even longer. "Five minutes to Epyc is an eternity." Mext technology aims to offload those infrequently accessed pages to flash. The challenge, Smerdon explains, is that while flash may be 50x cheaper per bit, 30x lower power per bit, it's also 500x slower. This is why most folks, when provisioning VPCs or servers, generally avoid swapping out to disk wherever possible: it kills application performance and sends service level agreements out the window. So for Mext's tech to work, it needed to ensure that any pages offloaded to storage were back in DRAM before they're needed. Kind of like running an errand in the middle of the workday – so long as you're back before your boss needs you again, they'll never know you left your desk. The problem was that the "R" in DRAM stands for random. Predicting which pages the system was going to need at which time isn't exactly trivial. The solution? (Brace for it.) "We realized we could use AI to monitor the system and proactively push those pages back into DRAM, so that as far as the application or the operating system knew, they were there the whole time," Smerdon said. In other words: "We transparently make flash appear as DRAM." So, "instead of buying two terabytes of DRAM for your Epyc-based server, you could buy one terabyte of DRAM, and then the next terabyte comes with Mext." To do this, AMD’s Mext employs a number of machine learning algorithms. "The workhorse model is a transformer derivative model, just like ChatGPT or Claude or the other famous models, but instead of predicting, for example, in the case of text, what word is next, what we're doing is predicting what page of memory is going to be required next," Smerdon explained. technology.title: UK's 'buy British' tech ambitions hit reality as less than £1 in £6 stays at home
technology.description: The UK government talks a good game about buying British, but less than £1 in every £6 spent with its biggest technology suppliers goes to British firms, according to research exposing how much Whitehall relies on foreign tech. A report from the Institute for Public Policy Research (IPPR) found that while 42.5 percent of spending with the public sector's 150 largest technology suppliers appears to go to UK companies, that figure collapses to just 15.4 percent once you look beyond where those businesses happen to be headquartered. A UK headquarters doesn't necessarily make a company British. Some are owned from overseas, others have most of their staff abroad, and many simply resell technology from US giants such as Microsoft. In fact, 43 percent of the spending attributed to UK-headquartered suppliers goes to resellers. Bytes and Softcat alone account for around £2 billion, making them two of the three biggest recipients of public sector technology spending. Once researchers traced reseller contracts back to the companies behind the products, the US emerged as the biggest beneficiary, accounting for £9.2 billion of the £19.2 billion spent with the largest suppliers. And the money isn't exactly being spread around. Just 150 companies receive 83 percent of public sector technology spending, with the largest 15 accounting for almost half. Smaller suppliers aren't getting much of a look-in either, receiving just 12 percent of government technology spending compared with 27 percent of spending across government as a whole. Competition is another concern. According to IPPR, 89.9 percent of government IT contracts over the past 12 months had no published record of how many suppliers bid for the work, making it difficult to assess how competitive those procurements were. Things get murkier when AI enters the picture, naturally. Government spending records show relatively little money going directly to the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic, but that doesn't mean Whitehall isn't buying their technology. Much of it is bundled into existing cloud agreements, enterprise software licenses, and partnerships. One example is NHS England's rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot to 505,000 staff , which IPPR says was carried out under a national licensing agreement signed in June 2023, before Copilot was even generally available. That means AI tools can reach hundreds of thousands of public sector workers through deals negotiated before those products were on the market, potentially leaving rival suppliers without an opportunity to compete. The report, Locked In: A Realist's Agenda for Digital Sovereignty, warns that Britain's dependence on American technology could become particularly troublesome if Washington restricts access to advanced AI systems.
